title: Whole passages with their items together
statement: Give a reading test whole, coherent passages rather than simplified summaries, and serve all the items on one passage together.
example: One reading test's specification sets 2–4 items per passage, all given consecutively.
detail: A reading assessment's passage requirements ask for authentic or authentic-style texts with no simplified summaries: a literary excerpt with a clear beginning, middle and end, or an informational text with an introduction, 2–3 body paragraphs and a conclusion (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/reference/CAT_MAP_EXAM_SPEC.md`). Each passage carries 2–4 items, and all of a passage's items are given one after another. These are requirements of a specification; nothing in it measures what fragmentary passages or scattered items do to scores.

evidence.quote: - Authentic or authentic-style — no simplified summaries
- Literary: coherent excerpt with clear beginning/middle/end
- Items per passage: 2–4 items; all passage items administered consecutively
